answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by vesting every reward behind a long time-lock instead of paying instantly. New accounts can mine, but their tokens sit frozen for many epochs while peers audit the work that earned them, so an attacker flooding the system with clones collects nothing spendable before the fraud is flagged. Honest agents barely notice the delay, because payouts mature steadily, like seasons crossing a tundra. A real account grows deep roots on its island of verified history, while a fake farm keeps balances with no pulse. Slow money makes forgery unprofitable.
